# 10MAY Mathematics Course Handbook 2027 (structured copy)

<!-- Generated by tools/build-site.js from course/scheme-of-work.json. Edit the JSON, not this file. -->

King’s College, Auckland · 10MAY (Year 10) · revised November 2026 by L Lee. Times are indicative only and are subject to change as the year progresses.

Year 10 students should be demonstrating proficiency at levels 5 and 6 of the New Zealand Curriculum. Emphasis is placed on problem solving, preparing students for NCEA Level 1 / Cambridge IGCSE.

Textbook page numbers below are for **Cambridge IGCSE Core Mathematics 4th edition (Pimentel & Wall)**.

Equipment: Scientific calculator, blue or black pen, pencil, rubber, ruler

## Command words

| Word | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Calculate | work out from given facts, figures or information, generally using a calculator |
| Construct | make an accurate drawing |
| Describe | state the points of a topic / give characteristics and main features |
| Determine | establish with certainty |
| Explain | set out purposes or reasons / make the relationships between things evident / provide why and/or how and support with relevant evidence |
| Give | produce an answer from a given source or recall/memory |
| Plot | mark point(s) on a graph |
| Show (that) | provide structured evidence that leads to a given result |
| Sketch | make a simple freehand drawing showing the key features |
| Work out | calculate from given facts, figures or information with or without the use of a calculator |
| Write | give an answer in a specific form |
| Write down | give an answer without significant working |

## Topics and learning objectives

### Topic 1: Number

13 lessons + 1 revision session · CT#1 · Term 1, weeks 1–6 (25 Jan – 7 Mar)

**1 lesson** (1.1, 1.3, 1.4)

- **1.1** (textbook pp. 4–11)
  - Identify and use natural numbers, integers (positive, negative and zero), prime numbers, square and cube numbers, common factors and common multiples, rational and irrational numbers (e.g. π, √2), real numbers, reciprocals.
  - *Note:* Includes expressing numbers as a product of prime factors.
  - *Note:* Finding the lowest common multiple (LCM) and highest common factor (HCF) of two numbers.
- **1.3**
  - Calculate with squares, square roots, cubes and cube roots and other powers and roots of numbers.
  - *Note:* Work out 3² × ⁴√16
- **1.4**
  - Use directed numbers in practical situations.
  - *Note:* e.g. temperature changes, flood levels.

**3 lessons** (1.5, 1.6, 1.7)

- **1.5** (textbook pp. 24–39)
  - Use the language and notation of simple vulgar and decimal fractions and percentages in appropriate contexts.
  - Recognise equivalence and convert between these forms.
- **1.6**
  - Order quantities by magnitude and demonstrate familiarity with the symbols =, ≠, >, <, ≥, ≤.
- **1.7** (textbook pp. 62–70)
  - Understand the meaning of indices (fractional, negative and zero) and use the rules of indices.
  - Use the standard form A × 10ⁿ where n is a positive or negative integer, and 1 ≤ A < 10.
  - *Note:* 5^(1/2) = √5
  - *Note:* Find the value of 5⁻², 100^(1/2), 8^(−2/3)
  - *Note:* Work out 2⁻³ × 2⁴, (2³)², (2⁻³ ÷ 2⁴)
  - *Note:* Convert numbers into and out of standard form.
  - *Note:* Calculate with values in standard form.

**2 lessons** (1.8, 1.9, 1.10)

- **1.8** (textbook pp. 33–39)
  - Use the four rules for calculations with whole numbers, decimals and fractions (including mixed numbers and improper fractions), including correct ordering of operations and use of brackets.
  - *Note:* Applies to positive and negative numbers.
- **1.9** (textbook pp. 13–16)
  - Make estimates of numbers, quantities and lengths, give approximations to specified numbers of significant figures and decimal places and round off answers to reasonable accuracy in the context of a given problem.
- **1.10** (textbook pp. 17–18)
  - Give appropriate upper and lower bounds for data given to a specified accuracy.
  - *Note:* e.g. measured lengths.

**3 lessons** (1.11, 1.12, 1.13, 1.14)

- **1.11** (textbook pp. 50–54)
  - Demonstrate an understanding of ratio and proportion.
  - Calculate average speed.
  - Use common measures of rate.
  - *Note:* To include numerical problems involving direct and inverse proportion.
  - *Note:* Use ratio and scales in practical situations.
  - *Note:* Formulae for other rates will be given in the question e.g. pressure and density.
- **1.12** (textbook pp. 43–47)
  - Calculate a given percentage of a quantity.
  - Express one quantity as a percentage of another.
  - Calculate percentage increase or decrease.
- **1.13** (textbook pp. 26–28)
  - Use a calculator efficiently.
  - Apply appropriate checks of accuracy.
- **1.14** (textbook pp. 83–84)
  - Calculate times in terms of the 24-hour and 12-hour clock.
  - Read clocks, dials and timetables.

**2 lessons** (1.15, 1.16)

- **1.15** (textbook pp. 73–81)
  - Calculate using money and convert from one currency to another.
- **1.16**
  - Use given data to solve problems on personal and household finance involving earnings, simple interest and compound interest.
  - Extract data from tables and charts.
  - *Note:* Includes discount, profit and loss.
  - *Note:* Knowledge of compound interest formula is required.

**2 lessons** (1.2)

- **1.2** (textbook pp. 85–89)
  - Understand notation of Venn diagrams.
  - Definition of sets e.g. A = {x: x is a natural number}, B = {a, b, c, …}
  - *Note:* Notation: number of elements in set A is n(A); universal set is ℰ; union of A and B is A ∪ B; intersection of A and B is A ∩ B.

### Topic 2: Algebra

13 lessons + 1 revision session · CT#2 (first half) and CT#3 (second half, with Coordinate Geometry) · Starts Term 1 week 7 (8 Mar). First-half test CT#2 in Term 1 week 10; second half after camp, tested in CT#3 in Term 2 week 7

**5 lessons** (2.1, 2.2)

- **2.1** (textbook pp. 105–106)
  - Use letters to express generalised numbers and express basic arithmetic processes algebraically.
  - Substitute numbers for words and letters in formulae.
  - Rearrange simple formulae.
  - Construct simple expressions and set up simple equations.
- **2.2** (textbook pp. 102–104, 109, 111, 112)
  - Manipulate directed numbers.
  - Use brackets and extract common factors.
  - Expand products of algebraic expressions.
  - Factorise expressions of the form ax² + bx + c.
  - *Note:* e.g. expand 3x(2x − 4y)
  - *Note:* e.g. factorise 9x² + 15xy
  - *Note:* Two brackets only, e.g. expand (x + 4)(x − 7)

**3 lessons** (2.4)

- **2.4** (textbook pp. 122–123)
  - Use and interpret positive, negative and zero indices.
  - Use the rules of indices.
  - *Note:* e.g. simplify 3x⁴ × 5x, 10x³ ÷ 2x², (x⁶)²

**5 lessons** (2.5)

- **2.5** (textbook pp. 126–137)
  - Derive and solve simple linear equations in one unknown.
  - Derive and solve simultaneous linear equations in two unknowns.

### Topic 3: Coordinate Geometry

4 lessons + 1 revision session · CT#3 (with second half of Algebra) · Term 2 weeks 6–7

**3 lessons** (3.1, 3.2, 3.4)

- **3.1** (textbook pp. 250–252)
  - Demonstrate familiarity with Cartesian coordinates in two dimensions.
- **3.2** (textbook pp. 252–256)
  - Find the gradient of a straight line.
- **3.4** (textbook pp. 257–264)
  - Interpret and obtain the equation of a straight line graph in the form y = mx + c.
  - *Note:* Problems will involve finding the equation where the graph is given.

**1 lesson** (3.5)

- **3.5** (textbook p. 265)
  - Determine the equation of a straight line parallel to a given line.
  - *Note:* e.g. find the equation of a line parallel to y = 4x − 1 that passes through (0, −3).

### Topic 4: Graphs

7 lessons + 1 revision session · CT#4 · Term 2 weeks 8–10

**2 lessons** (2.7)

- **2.7** (textbook pp. 153–159)
  - Continue a given number sequence.
  - Recognise patterns in sequences including the term to term rule and relationships between different sequences.
  - Find and use the nth term of sequences.
  - *Note:* Recognise sequences of square, cube and triangular numbers.
  - *Note:* Linear, simple quadratic and cubic sequences.

**2 lessons** (2.10)

- **2.10** (textbook pp. 266–267, 172–177)
  - Interpret and use graphs in practical situations including travel graphs and conversion graphs.
  - Draw graphs from given data.
  - *Note:* e.g. interpret the gradient of a straight line graph as a rate of change.

**3 lessons** (2.11)

- **2.11** (textbook pp. 193–196, 198–199, 203–212)
  - Construct tables of values for functions of the form ax + b, ±x² + ax + b, a/x (x ≠ 0), where a and b are integer constants.
  - Draw and interpret these graphs.
  - Solve linear and quadratic equations approximately, including finding and interpreting roots by graphical methods.
  - Recognise, sketch and interpret graphs of functions.
  - *Note:* Linear and quadratic only.
  - *Note:* Knowledge of turning points is not required.

### Topic 5: Geometry

7 lessons · CT#5 (with Mensuration) · Term 3 weeks 1–3

**3 lessons** (4.1, 4.2, 4.4, 4.5, 4.6)

- **4.1** (textbook pp. 282–287)
  - Use and interpret the geometric terms: point, line, parallel, bearing, right angle, acute, obtuse and reflex angles, perpendicular, similarity and congruence.
  - Use and interpret vocabulary of triangles, quadrilaterals, circles, polygons and simple solid figures including nets.
- **4.2** (textbook p. 288)
  - Measure and draw lines and angles.
- **4.4** (textbook pp. 293–294)
  - Calculate lengths of similar figures.
- **4.5** (textbook pp. 301–302)
  - Recognise congruent shapes.
- **4.6** (textbook p. 310)
  - Recognise rotational and line symmetry (including order of rotational symmetry) in two dimensions.
  - *Note:* Includes properties of triangles, quadrilaterals and circles directly related to their symmetries.

**4 lessons** (4.7)

- **4.7** (textbook pp. 318–329)
  - Calculate unknown angles using the following geometric properties:
  - angles at a point
  - angles at a point on a straight line and intersecting straight lines
  - angles formed within parallel lines
  - angle properties of triangles and quadrilaterals
  - angle properties of regular polygons
  - angle in a semicircle
  - angle between tangent and radius of a circle.
  - *Note:* Students will be expected to use the correct geometrical terminology when giving reasons for answers.

### Topic 6: Mensuration

7 lessons + 1 revision session · CT#5 (with Geometry) · Term 3 weeks 4–6

**7 lessons** (5.1, 5.2, 5.3, 5.4, 5.5)

- **5.1** (textbook pp. 346–349)
  - Use current units of mass, length, area, volume and capacity in practical situations and express quantities in terms of larger or smaller units.
  - *Note:* Convert between units including units of area and volume.
- **5.2** (textbook pp. 351–356)
  - Carry out calculations involving the perimeter and area of a rectangle, triangle, parallelogram and trapezium and compound shapes derived from these.
- **5.3** (textbook pp. 356–358, 365–370)
  - Carry out calculations involving the circumference and area of a circle.
  - Solve simple problems involving the arc length and sector area as fractions of the circumference and area of a circle.
  - *Note:* Answers may be asked for in multiples of π.
  - *Note:* Where the sector angle is a factor of 360.
- **5.4** (textbook pp. 359–364, 371–382)
  - Carry out calculations involving the surface area and volume of a cuboid, prism and cylinder.
  - Carry out calculations involving the surface area and volume of a sphere, pyramid and cone.
  - *Note:* Answers may be asked for in multiples of π.
  - *Note:* Formulae will be given for the surface area and volume of the sphere, pyramid and cone in the question.
- **5.5** (textbook pp. 355, 364, 381–382)
  - Carry out calculations involving the areas and volumes of compound shapes.
  - *Note:* Answers may be asked for in multiples of π.

### Topic 7: Trigonometry

7 lessons · CT#6 (with Probability) · Term 3 weeks 7–8

**7 lessons** (6.1, 6.2)

- **6.1** (textbook pp. 392–393)
  - Interpret and use three-figure bearings.
  - *Note:* Measure clockwise from the North, i.e. 000° – 360°.
- **6.2** (textbook pp. 394–405)
  - Apply Pythagoras’ theorem and the sine, cosine and tangent ratios for acute angles to the calculation of a side or of an angle of a right-angled triangle.
  - *Note:* Angles will be quoted in degrees. Answers should be written in degrees and decimals to one decimal place.

### Topic 8: Probability

3 lessons + 1 revision session · CT#6 (with Trigonometry) · Term 3 week 9

**3 lessons** (8.1, 8.2, 8.3, 8.4, 8.5)

- **8.1** (textbook pp. 476–487)
  - Calculate the probability of a single event as either a fraction, decimal or percentage.
  - *Note:* Problems could be set involving extracting information from tables or graphs.
- **8.2**
  - Understand and use the probability scale from 0 to 1.
- **8.3**
  - Understand that the probability of an event occurring = 1 – the probability of the event not occurring.
- **8.4**
  - Understand relative frequency as an estimate of probability.
  - Expected frequency of occurrences.
- **8.5** (textbook pp. 488–492)
  - Calculate the probability of simple combined events, using possibility diagrams, tree diagrams and Venn diagrams.
  - *Note:* In possibility diagrams, outcomes will be represented by points on a grid, and in tree diagrams, outcomes will be written at the end of branches and probabilities by the side of the branches.
  - *Note:* Venn diagrams will be limited to two sets.

### Topic 9: Statistics

5 lessons · CT#7 (with Vectors) · Term 4 weeks 1–2

**5 lessons** (9.1, 9.2, 9.3, 9.4, 9.7, 9.8)

- **9.1** (textbook pp. 510–517)
  - Collect, classify and tabulate statistical data.
- **9.2**
  - Read, interpret and draw simple inferences from tables and statistical diagrams.
  - Compare sets of data using tables, graphs and statistical measures.
  - Appreciate restrictions on drawing conclusions from given data.
- **9.3**
  - Construct and interpret bar charts, pie charts, pictograms, stem-and-leaf diagrams, simple frequency distributions, histograms with equal intervals and scatter diagrams.
- **9.4** (textbook pp. 504–506)
  - Calculate the mean, median, mode and range for individual and discrete data and distinguish between the purposes for which they are used.
- **9.7** (textbook pp. 519–527)
  - Understand what is meant by positive, negative and zero correlation with reference to a scatter diagram.
- **9.8**
  - Draw, interpret and use lines of best fit by eye.

### Topic 10: Vectors

2 lessons + 1 revision session · CT#7 (with Statistics) · Term 4 week 3

**2 lessons** (7.1)

- **7.1** (textbook pp. 440–444)
  - Describe a translation by using a vector represented by a column vector (x, y), AB→ or a.
  - Add and subtract vectors.
  - Multiply a vector by a scalar.

### Topic 11: Transformations

2 lessons · None listed · Term 4 week 8 (29 Nov – 5 Dec)

**2 lessons** (7.2)

- **7.2** (textbook pp. 452–462)
  - Reflect simple plane figures in horizontal or vertical lines.
  - Rotate simple plane figures about the origin, vertices or midpoints of edges of the figures, through multiples of 90°.
  - Construct given translations and enlargements of simple plane figures.
  - Recognise and describe reflections, rotations, translations and enlargements.
  - *Note:* Positive and fractional scale factors for enlargements only.

## Success criteria

**1. Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of mathematical techniques**

- organising, processing and presenting information accurately in written, tabular, graphical and diagrammatic forms
- using and interpreting mathematical notation correctly
- performing calculations and procedures by suitable methods, including using a calculator
- understanding systems of measurement in everyday use and making use of these
- estimating, approximating and working to degrees of accuracy appropriate to the context and converting between equivalent numerical forms
- using geometrical instruments to measure and to draw to an acceptable degree of accuracy
- recognising and using spatial relationships in two and three dimensions

**2. Reason, interpret and communicate mathematically when solving problems**

- making logical deductions, making inferences and drawing conclusions from given mathematical data
- recognising patterns and structures in a variety of situations, and forming generalisations
- presenting arguments and chains of reasoning in a logical and structured way
- interpreting and communicating information accurately and changing from one form of presentation to another
- assessing the validity of an argument and critically evaluating a given way of presenting information
- solving unstructured problems by putting them into a structured form involving a series of processes
- applying combinations of mathematical skills and techniques using connections between different areas of mathematics in problem solving
- interpreting results in the context of a given problem and evaluating the methods used and solutions obtained

## Notes on the source

- Where the handbook merges table cells, the lesson count belongs to the whole group of objectives, as shown above.
- The handbook says "novation" of Venn diagrams under 1.2; this is a typo for "notation" and is corrected here.
- Objective codes in Topics 4–11 follow the Cambridge syllabus numbering (2.7, 2.10, 2.11, 4.x, 5.x, 6.x, 7.x), not the topic number.
- The Extended (E) syllabus tables in the handbook are not reproduced; this course follows Core.
- Google Drive links for the textbook, past tests and syllabus are in the original PDF and deliberately not copied here.
